title-proc.eng: Copenhagen - New Metroline, M5 Civil Works South

description-proc.eng: This tender presents a substantial opportunity for prospective contractors to bid for the M5 Civil Works South (CWS) package, an important component of the Copenhagen metro system's expansion. This project is of significant strategic importance, as the M5 line is a fully automated driverless metro system that will not only enhance passenger service on existing metro corridors but also extend connectivity to emerging urban development areas, including Kløverparken, Refshaleøen, and Lynetteholm in the East Harbour. The M5 is designed to operate as an independent system, ensuring that its construction and subsequent operation do not disrupt the existing M1-M4 metro lines. MAIN COMPONENTS OF THE M5 CIVIL WORK The M5 south consists of approx 6.5 km twin bored tunnels, 5 underground stations(incl. 3 transfer stations),2 underground crossovers,5 cross passages,1 ramp, approx 2.0 km viaduct,1 elevated station, 1 viaduct cross-over,1 elevated bifurcation, short embankment sections. For further details on scope ref. is made to M5-2.1-CMBS-SW and M5-2.2-CWS-SW PHASES: The current tender, Phase 1, encompasses the southern section of the line, from north-west of København H to north of v/Prags Boulevard, with an anticipated operational commencement in 2036. title-proc.eng: 10028448-Strengthening data methodologies and monitoring systems for Gender-inclusive urban mobility in Brazil

description-proc.eng: Brazil's public transport systems are currently facing a structural crisis, with ridership falling by more than 30% since 2019. This situation disproportionately affects women and people of color, who are the primary users of the system and depend on it for access to basic rights such as health, education, and employment. Insufficient spatial coverage and low service quality reinforce a downward spiral of declining revenue and social exclusion. The "Just Transition in Urban Mobility in Brazil" project, implemented by GIZ in partnership with the Ministry of Cities (MCid), aims to create the conditions to improve the quality of public transport with a focus on the specific needs of women, black and vulnerable people, in addition to including them in various positions in the system, to ensure that such groups participate in decision-making. The project addresses the lack of data-based evidence and gender-sensitive standards in national and local planning. By strengthening the knowledge of relevant stakeholders and anchoring equity criteria in national policies and monitoring systems, the project seeks to catalyze a structural shift towards an inclusive and evidence-based urban mobility governance in Brazil. GIZ intends to contract a service aim to strengthen capacities and develop procedures for data collection, processing and use, research methodologies and monitoring systems in urban mobility planning in Brazil at national and subnational levels, incorporating the needs of women, people of color and vulnerable groups. To achieve this goal, the specific objectives are: - Develop and validate data collection and processing procedures, as well as a research methodology, to systematically integrate the needs of the target group into urban mobility planning. - Design and validate a methodology for integrating multiple data sources to strengthen inclusive urban mobility planning, with a focus on the target group. - Deliver capacity-building activities for partners and strategic actors through training activities, including courses, training and innovative formats. - Provide technical advisory services to pilot cities and support the implementation of project activities within the scope of the contract.

title-proc.eng: 72,5 kV Blue GIS - installations

description-proc.nld: Alliander N.V. is voornemens om middels de onderhandelingsprocedure zonder aankondiging op grond van artikel 3.36 lid 1 sub c onder 2 Aanbestedingswet 2012 een raamovereenkomst te sluiten met Siemens Energy B.V. ten behoeve van de levering van 72,5 kV Blue GIS installaties. Uit marktonderzoek van Alliander is gebleken dat Siemens Energy B.V. de enige partij is die in staat is de installaties te leveren die aan de eisen en specificaties van Alliander voldoen. Alliander is voornemens vijf (5) nieuwe onderstations te (doen) realiseren. Daartoe is zij voornemens vijf (5) GIS schakelinstallaties in te kopen. Alliander heeft een aantal locaties beschikbaar waarop zij voornemens is de nieuwe onderstations te plaatsen. Deze onderstations zijn gepland voor realisatie na 1-1-2028. De selectie van de locaties voor deze onderstations heeft plaatsgevonden voor de ingang van de F-gassen verordening. Hierbij is rekening gehouden met de afmetingen van schakelinstallaties van het SF6-houdende soort. Uitbreiding van de locaties is niet mogelijk. Zij kan daarom enkel schakelinstallaties aanschaffen die binnen de afmetingen van deze locaties passen. Maximale afmetingen (BxDxH) per veld zijn: • Busbar: 800 x 4250 x 2870 mm • Transformer bay (50 kV transformer): 800 x 4470 x 2600 mm • Transformer bay (150/110 kV transformer): 800 x 5275 x 2870 mm • Cable bay: 800 x 4470 x 2600 mm • Busbar coupling bay: 800x 3650 x 2600 mm Het uitbreiden van de locaties is niet mogelijk.  Verder vereist Alliander een nominale rail  stroom van 3150A en 40 kArms / 3 s kortsluitvastheid. Op grond van de Europese F-gassenverordening is het Alliander in beginsel niet meer toegestaan om na 1-1-2028 SF6-houdende installaties in bedrijf te nemen met een spanningsniveau vanaf 52 kV tot en met 145 kV. Alliander heeft mede daarom de volgende eis geformuleerd waaraan het in de schakelinstallatie gebruikte isolatie- en blusmedium moet voldoen: ‘Gasmixtures with GWP ≤1 and vacuum (SF6 gas and PFAS are not permitted)’. Uitsluiting van het gebruik van PFAS-houdend gas (in het bijzonder C4FN) geschiedt om de volgende redenen die deze keuze ieder voor zich en alle tezamen legitimeren: 1. Minimalisatieplicht ZZS ten aanzien van het vrijkomen van Zeer Zorgwekkende Stoffen (ZZS), waaronder PFAS. 2. Zorgplicht voor personeel. Alliander heeft een zorgplicht gedurende de volledige levensduur van haar schakelinstallaties. Van PFAS-houdende gassen is bekend dat zij onomkeerbare gezondheidsrisico's met zich meebrengen. Schakelinstallaties zijn bovendien niet volledig lekvrij. Alliander wil haar personeel niet aan deze risico's blootstellen. 3. Bescherming van het milieu. Van PFAS-houdende gassen is bekend dat zij onomkeerbare risico's voor de natuur met zich brengen. Alliander wil geen onnodige schade toebrengen aan het milieu. 4. Uniformiteit. Alliander heeft op dit moment geen PFAS-houdende installaties in gebruik, waardoor haar personeel gedurende de volledige levensduur van dergelijke installaties specifiek hiervoor opgeleid en gecertificeerd zou moeten worden. Een eventueel toekomstig verbod zou het parallel in bedrijf houden van meerdere systemen leiden tot inefficiëntie in opleiding en inzet van personeel. Alliander wenst zo veel mogelijk uniformiteit in haar installaties te hebben en daarbij volledig in te zetten op toekomstbestendige keuzes.     5. Onzekerheid over beschikbaarheid op lange termijn. De installaties hebben een levensduur van ten minste 40 jaar, die in de praktijk kan oplopen tot 60 jaar en, in geval van lekkage, bijgevuld moeten worden met gas. De beschikbaarheid van PFAS-houdende gassen is op de lange termijn onzeker, waardoor de levensduur van de installaties significant ingekort zou kunnen worden. 6. Onvoldoende onderzoek naar C4FN. C4FN is een relatief nieuw ontwikkeld gas waarnaar nog onvoldoende onderzoek is gedaan. De onafhankelijke en afhankelijke onderzoeken geven nog geen eenduidig resultaat. Alliander wil geen technologie in gebruik nemen waarvan de risico's nog niet voldoende in kaart zijn gebracht. Isolatiemediums met GWP ≤1 en vacuüm (zonder SF6 en PFAS) bieden de zekerheid dat deze niet voornoemde risico’s voor milieu en gezondheid met zich brengen. Ook is geen verbod op deze technologie voorzien, waardoor de zekerheid bestaat dat installaties op basis van deze technologie gedurende de hele levensduur kunnen worden onderhouden. Op lange termijn is standaardisatie van schakelaars in het elektriciteitsnet een belangrijk uitgangspunt. Vanwege snel ontwikkelende regelgeving, is deze technologie het meest toekomstbestendig.    Geen redelijk alternatief of substituut Alliander heeft een marktonderzoek uitgevoerd waaruit bleek dat er geen andere partijen dan Siemens zijn die aan alle voornoemde eisen kunnen voldoen. De VT Blue GIS is de enige installatie aan alle eisen voldoet en die qua omvang past binnen de locaties die Alliander beschikbaar heeft om nieuwe stations te realiseren.  Voor alternatieve installaties die aan de andere eisen voldoen, zou ten minste 25% meer ruimte vereist zijn. Het aankopen van extra ruimte is niet mogelijk. description-proc.eng: Alliander N.V. intends to award a framework agreement to Siemens Energy B.V. through the negotiated procedure without prior publication pursuant to Article 3.36(1)(c)(2) of the Dutch Public Procurement Act 2012 for the supply of 72.5 kV Blue GIS installations. Market research conducted by Alliander has demonstrated that Siemens Energy B.V. is the only supplier capable of providing installations that meet Alliander’s requirements and specifications. Alliander intends to realize five (5) new substations. To that end, it intends to procure five (5) GIS switchgear installations. Alliander has identified a number of sites on which it intends to construct the new substations. These substations are scheduled to be commissioned after 1 January 2028. The selection of these sites took place prior to the entry into force of the F-gas Regulation and was based on the dimensions of SF₆-containing switchgear installations. Expansion of the sites is not possible. Consequently, Alliander can only procure switchgear installations that fit within the available site dimensions. The maximum dimensions (W × D × H) per bay are: • Busbar bay: 800 × 4250 × 2870 mm • Transformer bay (50 kV transformer): 800 × 4470 × 2600 mm • Transformer bay (150/110 kV transformer): 800 × 5275 × 2870 mm • Cable bay: 800 × 4470 × 2600 mm • Busbar coupling bay: 800 × 3650 × 2600 mm Furthermore, Alliander requires a nominal busbar current of 3150 A and a short-circuit withstand rating of 40 kArms / 3 s. Under the European F-gas Regulation, Alliander is, in principle, no longer permitted to commission SF₆-containing installations with voltage levels from 52 kV up to and including 145 kV after 1 January 2028. Accordingly, Alliander has formulated the following requirement for the insulation and interruption medium used in the switchgear installation: "Gas mixtures with GWP ≤1 and vacuum (SF₆ gas and PFAS are not permitted)." The exclusion of PFAS-containing gases (in particular C4FN) is justified by the following reasons, each of which individually and collectively supports this choice: 1. Minimalisatieplicht ZZS ten aanzien van het vrijkomen van Zeer Zorgwekkende Stoffen (ZZS). This includes PFAS, which are classified as substances of very high concern under Dutch environmental legislation. 2. Duty of care towards personnel. Alliander has a duty of care throughout the entire service life of its switchgear installations. PFAS-containing gases are known to pose irreversible health risks. Moreover, switchgear installations are not entirely leak-tight. Alliander does not wish to expose its personnel to these risks. 3. Environmental protection. PFAS-containing gases are known to pose irreversible risks to the environment. Alliander aims to avoid unnecessary environmental harm. 4. Standardization and uniformity. Alliander currently operates no PFAS-containing installations. Consequently, its personnel would need to be specifically trained and certified throughout the entire service life of such installations. A potential future prohibition could require the parallel operation of multiple technological systems, resulting in inefficiencies in personnel training and deployment. Alliander seeks to maintain maximum uniformity across its installations and to make future-proof technology choices. 5. Uncertainty regarding long-term availability. The installations have an expected service life of at least 40 years and, in practice, may remain in operation for up to 60 years. In the event of leakage, gas replenishment may be required. The long-term availability of PFAS-containing gases is uncertain, which could significantly shorten the operational lifespan of the installations. 6. Insufficient research on C4FN. C4FN is a relatively recently developed gas for which insufficient research has been conducted. Independent and industry-sponsored studies have not yet yielded consistent conclusions. Alliander does not wish to adopt technology whose risks have not yet been adequately assessed. Insulation media with a GWP ≤1 combined with vacuum interruption technology (excluding SF₆ and PFAS) provide assurance that the aforementioned environmental and health risks are avoided. Furthermore, no future ban on this technology is currently anticipated, providing confidence that installations based on this technology can be maintained throughout their entire service life. In the long term, standardization of switchgear technologies across the electricity network is an important objective. Given the rapidly evolving regulatory landscape, this technology represents the most future-proof solution. No Reasonable Alternative or Substitute Alliander conducted a market analysis which concluded that no supplier other than Siemens is capable of meeting all of the above requirements. The VT Blue GIS is the only installation that satisfies all requirements while also fitting within the space available at the identified substation sites. Alternative installations that satisfy the other technical requirements would require at least 25% more space. Acquiring additional land or expanding the available sites is not possible. Training programs for surgeons and clinical staff. Technical support and customer service. Guidance for patient follow-up and rehabilitation. Participation in this RFI or any subsequent market dialogue does not create any obligation for HUS to initiate a procurement procedure, award a contract, or compensate suppliers for any costs incurred in preparing responses or participating in discussions. Neither the request for information nor its replies are binding on either party. Responding to a request for information does not affect the position of the tenderer in the forthcoming tender. The information provided by suppliers may be used solely for planning and preparing a potential future procurement process in accordance with applicable procurement legislation. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Suppliers are requested to submit their responses electronically in English. Responses should include all relevant supporting documentation, including product brochures, technical specifications, clinical evidence, and regulatory documentation where available. title-proc.eng: EU Complementary Time (C-T) and Complementary Position and Navigation (C-PN) services

description-proc.eng: Satellite-based navigation and timing services are a cornerstone of Europe’s economy and critical infrastructure resilience. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications. Several studies attribute roughly 10 % of EU GDP to PNT related activities, while a single day without GNSS could have a financial impact up to €1 billion. The Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59). The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF. Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess: • How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU. • How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034. • How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required.

description-proc.eng: Nygårdstunnelen in Bergen was opened in 1999 and is 864 metres long. The tunnel runs from the Puddefjord Bridge to Nygårdstangen, with exit ramps at O.J. Brochsgate. There are 2 lanes from the Puddefjord Bridge, whilst there are 1 lanes from O.J. Brochs gate. These meet in the tunnel so that there are 3 lanes at the exit and entrance at Nygårdstangen. The annual daily traffic is approx. 45,000. The tunnel shall be upgraded in accordance with the tunnel safety regulations and equipment in and outside the tunnel shall be replaced and replaced with new equipment that meets the current requirements. This includes, among other things: • New ventilation system. • New lighting installations with both new lights in the tunnel roof and continuous evacuation lights. • Extinguishing water shall be set up for the fire brigade. New system for handling emissions and tunnel washing water that fulfils emission requirements. • New signage with barriers, lane signal and variable signs. • Emergency stations with fire extinguishers and telephones. • Camera with coverage throughout the entire tunnel, which gives an alarm during events. • New technical building in the tunnel in the existing mountain room. • A new stop section shall be established at the technical building. • Demolition of existing air treatment plant.
